sections.h2: What should McAllen owners weigh before choosing how to sell?
sections.html:
Repair costs, any claims on the title and the date you need cash usually settle the choice. McAllen prices are modest next to the Dallas suburbs, so a few thousand dollars of repairs or fees can be a large share of the result.

The Census Bureau estimated 150,640 residents on July 1, 2025, up 5.9 percent from 142,188 in the 2020 base. Growth is steady rather than explosive, and 28.2 percent of residents are under 18.

  • Hiring an agent brings the biggest buyer pool and the slowest timeline.
  • Going it alone saves the fee and hands you the forms.
  • A cash purchase skips repairs and showings, at a price below retail.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about McAllen housing and incomes?
sections.html:
McAllen is one of the lower-priced large cities in Texas. For 2020-2024 the median owner-occupied value was $190,400, median household income was $61,579 and the poverty rate was 20.0 percent.

About four in ten homes are rented, so tenant-occupied houses are part of the market. Workers spend 21.9 minutes on the road to work, the shortest trip among the four cities in this group. Retail sales per capita in 2022 were $34,416, a sign of the shopping trade the city draws from across the border region.

sections.h2: Where is McAllen, and how did it begin?
sections.html:
McAllen is on U.S. Highway 83 in southern Hidalgo County, so Hidalgo County offices handle its deeds and tax accounts. The Handbook of Texas traces the site to Spanish land grants of 1767 and the later McAllen Ranch.

The railroad reached the ranch on August 20, 1904, and a townsite company formed that December and named the town for John McAllen. A rival settlement called East McAllen grew two miles away. The town incorporated in 1911 and adopted a home rule charter in 1927.

A toll bridge to Reynosa opened in 1941, which made McAllen a port of entry and a winter tourist stop. The city took the nickname City of Palms and later hosted a foreign trade zone. The Handbook also notes that colonias of varying size ring the city, so a buyer may ask about utilities and lot status.

sections.h2: What local factors affect pricing a McAllen house?
sections.html:
Ask an inspector about the roof, cooling system and drainage before you list. A clear list of repair costs lets you compare offers on equal footing.

  • Check that the deed names every current owner, particularly where a house passed down a family without probate.
  • Ask the Hidalgo County tax office what the account owes, including older years.
  • Confirm homestead, over-65, disability or veteran exemptions with the Hidalgo appraisal district.

Census figures show 87.0 percent of McAllen residents identify as Hispanic or Latino, and 73.7 percent of people five and older use another language at home. Many transactions run in English and Spanish, so a bilingual title officer and translated documents can help a sale move along.

sections.h2: Can I rent out a McAllen house by the night?
sections.html:
Yes, but McAllen requires an annual registration for each rental unit. The city defines a short-term rental as use of a residential dwelling or accessory building for less than 30 consecutive days, and the environmental health and code compliance department handles the paperwork at the McAllen Development Center on North 15th Street.

If you are selling a house that guests have used, a buyer will want to know the registration is in good standing. The ordinance sets the rules a registrant must meet:

  • The annual registration fee is $100 per unit, and a registration lasts one year unless ownership changes.
  • The operator names a local contact who can be reached around the clock and who must respond in person within one hour to complaints.
  • Every sleeping space needs a working smoke detector, and a map of exits must be posted.
  • Operators file a monthly hotel occupancy tax report even in months with no bookings.

Breaking the article is a Class C misdemeanor, fined up to $500 for each offense, with every day treated as its own offense. The director may revoke a permit, after which the property cannot reapply for twelve months. The article also says registration does not override private deed restrictions, so check any HOA rules too.

sections.h2: How does eviction work if a McAllen house has a tenant?
sections.html:
Eviction starts with written notice to vacate, usually three days unless the lease says otherwise, and moves to justice court.

  • The court sets the hearing within a window of 10 to 21 days from filing.
  • Losing parties have 5 days from judgment to appeal to county court.
  • A writ of possession becomes available on day six after final judgment.

A tenant-occupied house can still sell, and many investors buy that way. If you want it empty at closing, plan the notice schedule before you sign a contract.

sections.h2: How do Hidalgo County appraisal notices and protests work for McAllen owners?
sections.html:
Each spring the Hidalgo County Appraisal District sends a Notice of Appraised Value to owners whose market value climbed by $1,000 or more. The notice lists three figures: market value as of January 1, the assessed or net appraised value after limits such as a homestead cap, and the taxable value after exemptions.

If the market value looks too high, the owner can protest it. The district's deadline is May 15 or 30 days after the notice is mailed, whichever is later, and a protest can be mailed or handed in at its office on South Professional Drive in Edinburg. After filing, the owner can see the district's evidence through an online account and meet an appraiser in an informal meeting. Anyone who declines the settlement offer goes before the Appraisal Review Board, and a family member or friend can represent you if you file an Appointment of Agent form.

For a seller, a lower value helps only the tax bill, not the sale price. A buyer still pays what the market bears, but a protest filed before closing can lower the tax prorated between you.

sections.h2: What if a McAllen owner is behind or has died?
sections.html: A sale that closes before a foreclosure auction can keep the equity with the owner and head off a deficiency suit. Inherited houses follow different tracks: a transfer on death deed recorded in the owner's lifetime avoids probate, while heirs without one may file a muniment of title or an affidavit of heirship, which a buyer can decline.

sections.h2: What do McAllen's Census numbers say about growth and health coverage?
sections.html:
McAllen's land area grew from 48.34 square miles in 2010 to 62.31 in 2020, while its population density slipped from 2,686.5 to 2,282.4 people per square mile, which fits a city that has annexed land. The 2025 estimate of 150,640 compares with 129,877 in 2010.

Households average 2.95 people, and 89.0 percent of residents lived at the same address a year earlier. The Census Bureau reports 26.9 percent of residents under 65 without health insurance and 8.5 percent with a disability, figures that help explain why some owners face medical bills alongside housing costs. About 95.9 percent of households have a computer and 92.2 percent have broadband.

faqs.a: Hidalgo County. The Handbook of Texas places McAllen in the southern part of the county, so Hidalgo County offices handle your deed and tax account.

faqs.q: What does the Census Bureau list as a McAllen home value?
faqs.a: The 2020-2024 estimate is $190,400 for an owned home. Repairs, size and age move any single house away from that figure.

faqs.q: Can I sell an inherited McAllen house without probate?
faqs.a: Sometimes, if the owner recorded a transfer on death deed beforehand. Without one, heirs choose among probate, a muniment of title and an affidavit of heirship.

faqs.q: How fast can a landlord remove a tenant in Texas?
faqs.a: Expect a hearing 10 to 21 days after filing, then a writ of possession from day six after judgment. Appeals have a 5 day limit.

faqs.q: Does selling help if I am behind on my mortgage?
faqs.a: It can, when closing comes before the auction. Proceeds pay the lien first. Ask the servicer for a payoff statement.
